<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914964_theRebbe_974" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914964_theRebbe_974__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the connection between the two interpretations of "the life of Sarah" and how being the master over one's life enables all years to be equal for good, linking this to the concept of teshuvah from love which transcends time.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, it was explained above</t>
    <t s="2">(section 2)</t>
    <t s="3">the connection and relationship of the two interpretations in "the life of Sarah"</t>
    <t s="4">("her life was good, and all were equal for good"),</t>
    <t s="5">that through the fact that the life is "her own,"</t>
    <t s="6">meaning she is the master over all her life,</t>
    <t s="7">she is able to effect that all</t>
    <t s="8">(all her years,</t>
    <t s="9">even the years of the past)</t>
    <t s="10">be equal for good.</t>
    <t s="11">And we need to understand the connection of this matter of "her life was good"</t>
    <t s="12">(that she is the master over all her years of life)</t>
    <t s="13">with what is explained in the maamar, that the concept of "her life was good" is that even the sensed is in a state of nullification.</t>
    <t s="14">And we can explain this based on what is explained elsewhere,</t>
    <t s="15">that through teshuvah</t>
    <t s="16">(from love)</t>
    <t s="17">a change is made in the past,</t>
    <t s="18">because the root of time is in Malchus,</t>
    <t s="19">and higher than that is the precedence and delay in the order of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="20">and since teshuvah is above the chain of descent</t>
    <t s="21">(in man,</t>
    <t s="22">therefore the revelation drawn down through teshuvah is a revelation that is above the chain of descent),</t>
    <t s="23">therefore the limitations of past, present, and future do not apply to it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that although teshuvah occurs in a specific moment of time, because teshuvah itself transcends time, it draws the transcendence of time into the moment, thereby enabling a change in the past.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And even though the act of teshuvah itself is in a specific moment that is limited by the definition of time,</t>
    <t s="1">past, present, and future,</t>
    <t s="2">and from the perspective of the definition of time it is impossible that an action in the present could change the past</t>
    <t s="3">(because a cause must precede its effect),</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="5">since teshuvah itself is above the limitation of time,</t>
    <t s="6">therefore,</t>
    <t s="7">through it is drawn the transcendence of time into time itself</t>
    <t s="8">(into the moment of performing teshuvah),</t>
    <t s="9">and it is as if this moment was earlier,</t>
    <t s="10">before the effect.</t>
    <t s="11">And based on this we can explain the connection of the two concepts in "her life was good"</t>
    <t s="12">[that even the sensed is in a state of nullification,</t>
    <t s="13">and that she is the master over all her years of life],</t>
    <t s="14">that through the sensed</t>
    <t s="15">(existence,</t>
    <t s="16">limitation)</t>
    <t s="17">being in a state of nullification</t>
    <t s="18">(above existence and limitation),</t>
    <t s="19">through this,</t>
    <t s="20">even into time</t>
    <t s="21">(limitation)</t>
    <t s="22">is drawn the transcendence that is above time.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section concludes that the concept of "her life was good" serves as a lesson and empowerment for every Jew to serve G-d with joy in the revealed and sensed, while remaining in a state of nullification, thereby enhancing the power of teshuvah to change the past.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And even though this matter</t>
    <t s="2">(that the sensed is in a state of nullification)</t>
    <t s="3">is a lofty level,</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="5">since the deeds of the Patriarchs and Matriarchs are a sign and empowerment for the children,</t>
    <t s="6">the concept of "her life was good" that was with Sarah is a lesson and empowerment for every Jew that he can serve G-d with joy in the revealed and sensed, and that nevertheless he will not come from this to a feeling of self-existence,</t>
    <t s="7">because even his sensed is in a state of nullification</t>
    <t s="8">(as above, section 6).</t>
    <t s="9">And through joy in the service of G-d in general,</t>
    <t s="10">and in particular when the joy is in the service of teshuvah itself</t>
    <t s="11">[as explained elsewhere</t>
    <t s="12">that the joy of a mitzvah applies also to the mitzvah of teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="13">and on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="14">the joy of the mitzvah of teshuvah is greater than the joy of all other mitzvos],</t>
    <t s="15">through this the power of teshuvah is further increased to also change the past.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
